title: Derived cohomology preserves exact coproducts
statement: Let C be an abelian category with a derived category and K-injective resolutions. Let I be any indexing type such that coproducts of shape Discrete I exist and are exact in C. For every integer q, the derived homology functor H^q : D(C) → C preserves coproducts of shape Discrete I. No boundedness or nonemptiness condition is imposed on the family.

source.place: Section Homology, instance preservesColimitsOfShape_homologyFunctor; Stacks Injectives Tag 07D9, coproduct clauses (1)-(2).

proof.text: Use the already-proved source instance DerivedCategory.preservesColimitsOfShape_homologyFunctor. Represent each member of the derived family by a cochain complex. Localization of their termwise coproduct is a coproduct in D(C), by computing maps into K-injective targets. Exactness of coproducts makes cochain homology preserve this coproduct, via pointwise short-complex homology. Transport its colimit cocone through homologyFunctorFactors and the representative isomorphisms. The transports preserve the specified coprojections. This includes the empty family. This node attaches the existing complete source proof and introduces no Lean obligation.
